If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $x=3-(y-3)^{2},\,$ $x=(y-3)^{2}+4,$ $y=0,$ and $y=3,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type II region. To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14055472/assets/3191f16e4c72739688fa4243b44a374a027b307b6e4d419217545e924e1c7a4a.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,3-(y-3)^{2}\le x\le (y-3)^{2}+4}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{3-(y-3)^{2}}^{(y-3)^{2}+4}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{3-(y-3)^{2}}^{(y-3)^{2}+4}f(x,y)\,dx]dy\end{aligned}
$$
